data.title: Šurany in the 16th century in 3D
data.excerpt: Šurany is first mentioned in a charter of the Hungarian king Béla II of 3 September 1138 as “villa Suran”, and by the second half of the 14th century a castle stood here to which 12 villages and hamlets belonged. Our 3D visualisation shows the town and the adjoining castle at the height of their prosperity in the 16th century.

children.text: the website of the town of Šurany

states, Šurany is first mentioned in a charter of the Hungarian king Béla II of 3 September 1138 as “villa Suran”. By the second half of the 14th century Šurany Castle already stood here and 12 villages and hamlets belonged to it.

In 1663 – 1684 it was occupied by the Ottomans and in 1725 it was largely demolished. Among the important figures connected with this castle were the castle captain Baron Tomáš Bosniak and his daughter Žofia. Her incorrupt body (she died on 28 April 1644) rested – until it was destroyed by a psychopath – in the Loreto chapel at Teplička nad Váhom near Strečno, where she lived with her husband Fraňo Wesselényi.

and hradiska.sk, on the occasion of the Museum Night event held on 20 May 2017, attempted in cooperation with the Town Museum in Šurany to create a 3D visualisation of the possible appearance of the town of Šurany and the adjoining castle in the period of its prosperity in the 16th century. In creating the model we drew on material by RNDr. Miroslav Eliáš (Eliáš, Miroslav. Pamätný spis k dejinám Šurianskeho hradu. - 1st ed. - Šurany: Mestské kultúrne stredisko, 2006) and consulted the details with him. Another important source was the First Military Survey of Hungary, on which the urban layout of the town in the 18th century is still clearly visible and on which the ruin (Rudera) of the by then vanished castle is also marked. The Second Military Survey of the mid-19th century no longer recorded this ruin, even though that survey is generally far more precise than the first. It is therefore likely that by this period the castle no longer showed even the signs of a clearly visible ruin.
